primary_account: @ai._kid (claura-ai.com) — the target brand system to steal structure from
note_on_corpus: The 83 refs are NOT all from @ai._kid. Roughly 35-40% are @ai._kid (cream/terracotta/warm-black editorial system). The rest are adjacent AI-creator accounts mixed in for pattern-mining: @francisco.carosia (3D chunky mascot, same cream/terracotta palette), @ramiro.cubria (full dark-bg, voxel 3D character team), @juanbertorello.ia (paper-grain cream, GitHub-repo showcase cards), a brutalist blueprint/poster series (voxel mascot, orange+black+cream newsprint, corner registration crosses — handle not visible in crop), @soydiegoosorio (3D realistic avatar, orange starburst stickers), a '42 skills/7 crews' deck with pastel department colors (handle not fully visible), @rifqieh (light-grey bg, no cream/terracotta at all — excluded from core DNA), and @luzzidigital (cooler grey stucco bg — excluded from core DNA). This file documents the CORE system (@ai._kid + its closest cousins on the same cream/terracotta palette) and flags the outliers separately.

background_cream.notes: warm parchment/off-white, very subtle grain/paper texture visible on close zoom. This is the dominant canvas color across ~90% of core-system slides.

background_cream_alt_grid.notes: same family, seen with a faint dot/grid texture in a few slides (juanbertorello variant).

terracotta_accent.notes: the single signature accent color. Used for: italic serif accent words in headlines, CTA pill fills, diamond/dot bullet markers, stat numbers, thin dividers, small icons (paperclip/link glyph), progress-dot highlight.

terracotta_deep.notes: slightly deeper variant seen in some CTA buttons/pills — likely the same token at a different render or a hover/pressed state.

warm_black.notes: near-black with a warm brown undertone, never pure #000. Used for headline serif text (non-accent words), bold body emphasis, and as the fill of dark UI/terminal mockup cards embedded inside cream slides.

mockup_dark_bg.notes: the embedded 'app/terminal' card background — distinct from warm_black, cooler/flatter, used only inside the dashboard-mockup cards (macOS traffic-light dots, code, tables).

blush_secondary.notes: a soft dusty-rose/blush used as the fill for kicker badges ('01/08 — AGENTE 1') and for one CTA highlight block. Reads as cream + terracotta mixed at low saturation.

success_green.notes: used sparingly and only inside dark mockups — 'listo', '92%', checkmarks, positive deltas. Never used on the cream background itself.

white.notes: card backgrounds on the few slides with a light-grey canvas (secondary accounts), and mockup text/UI chrome.

color.teal_check: NOT PRESENT as a brand color. The only teal/green-blue pixel found in the whole set is the native WhatsApp header chrome inside one screenshotted phone-UI mockup (ref-20) — that is real-app furniture being depicted, not a brand choice. Confirmed: the @ai._kid / core system palette is cream + terracotta + warm-black only, no teal.
color.incidental_purple: Purple/violet appears twice, both inside embedded DARK UI mockup graphics (a 'command center' network-sphere illustration, and a rainbow-colored folder-tag stack illustration) — i.e. as content inside a screenshot-style card, not as a background or accent applied to typography/CTAs. Treat as decorative-mockup-only, not a core token.

outlier_palettes_excluded.note: no cream/terracotta at all, bold navy/black condensed sans headlines — excluded from core DNA
terracotta accent stickers but cooler grey base, not warm cream — excluded from core DNA

outlier_palettes_excluded.bg: pastel per-department (dusty rose, mauve, sage green, powder blue, grey)
outlier_palettes_excluded.note: each 'department' card slide gets its own muted pastel bg + matching pixel-mascot silhouette color — a distinct sub-system, catalogued as its own archetype below but not part of the core two-tone palette

serif_display.characteristics: transitional serif, moderate-high contrast, soft ball terminals, warm/humanist feel rather than cold Didone. Set in warm_black.

serif_display_italic.role: the accent word/phrase inside a headline (always terracotta), plus small italic footer notes ('desliza →', 'Automatizá tu marketing con IA') and italic stat numbers
serif_display_italic.characteristics: same family as serif_display, swashy/calligraphic italic with visible ink-trap flourish on some letterforms.

sans_grotesk_body.role: paragraph body copy, mockup UI text, card labels
sans_grotesk_body.characteristics: clean humanist grotesk, medium x-height, regular + bold weights used for in-line emphasis.

monospace.role: kicker/eyebrow tags ('01/08 — AGENTE 1 · ICP FINDER', 'EL BUILD'), terminal/code mockup content, small numeric captions, tag chips
monospace.characteristics: used almost always upper-case with slight letter-spacing for eyebrows; regular case for terminal content.

secondary_bold_grotesk_display.role: ONLY seen in adjacent/outlier accounts (rifqieh, brutalist poster series, juanbertorello '+50 skills'), not core ai._kid
secondary_bold_grotesk_display.characteristics: extra-bold condensed sans for shouty single-word or short-phrase headlines; flag as optional secondary voice, not primary.

type_scale_relationship.body_sans: ~22-26px, line-height ~1.4-1.5, bold inline spans for the 'so what' sentence

spacing_density.canvas: 1080×1350 px (4:5 vertical, native IG carousel ratio)
spacing_density.outer_margin: ~72-84px side margins (~7% of width) — generous, never edge-to-edge except decorative corner marks
spacing_density.vertical_rhythm: content blocks separated by 40-64px; header-zone to headline gap ~48-64px; headline to body ~24-32px; body to mockup card ~48-56px
spacing_density.density_read: airy/editorial, not cramped — roughly 1 headline + 1 short body graf + 1 visual proof per slide, rarely more

shape.border_radius_kicker_badge: 6-8px (slightly rounded rectangle, not a full pill)
shape.signature_shape_note: the fully-rounded terracotta CTA pill ('Comentá AGENTES', 'Comentá CRM') is the single most repeated shape — always centered, always terracotta fill, always white bold sans/serif label inside.

zone_structure: header zone: top-center or top-left small mono/serif site label with a link glyph (🔗 claura-ai.com), sometimes paired top-right with a small pill badge ('nadie lo cuenta') or slide-index ('01/08')
kicker zone (on detail slides): small badge + mono eyebrow line directly under header, above headline
hero/body zone: headline block (serif + italic terracotta accent) + short body paragraph, optionally a mascot illustration to the right
proof zone: an embedded dark-mode UI/terminal/dashboard mockup card, OR an icon grid, OR a stat row — this is the 'evidence' beat of the slide
stat-caption row: 2-3 short italic terracotta numbers with mono uppercase captions underneath, evenly spaced in columns
footer zone: handle bottom-left (plain bold sans, '@ai._kid'), short italic serif hook/CTA bottom-right ('siguiente →', 'te espero en comments ↓'), pagination dots centered at very bottom
layout_grid.carousel_chrome_note: left/right circular nav arrows visible mid-frame are Instagram's own UI chrome from the screenshot capture, not part of the authored design — do not replicate them as a design element, only the dot pagination is authored.

design_style.mood: confident, editorial, quietly premium — reads like a boutique newsletter or fashion-adjacent tech brand rather than a typical 'AI bro' dashboard aesthetic. Warm and human despite the technical subject matter.
design_style.personality: a mix of magazine-editorial (serif italics, generous whitespace) and terminal/builder credibility (embedded dark UI mockups, monospace kickers). The pairing of a delicate italic serif with raw terminal screenshots is the brand's central tension/signature.
design_style.composition_strategy: one idea per slide, strict hierarchy: kicker → headline (with exactly one italicized terracotta accent phrase) → one supporting sentence → one piece of visual proof (mockup/stat/icon-grid). Rarely more than 3 content beats per slide.
design_style.whitespace_usage: heavy, deliberate negative space above/below the headline block; the cream canvas is treated as a feature, not a gap to fill. Dark mockup cards are the only 'dense' element and are visually contained/framed to contrast against the airy cream field.
design_style.contrast_approach: primarily a light-on-light system (cream bg, warm-black text, single terracotta accent) punctuated by isolated dark-mode 'islands' (the mockup cards) that act as evidence/proof-of-work — the dark card is always a rectangle with soft shadow floating on the cream field, never the full-bleed background of a core ai._kid slide.
design_style.accent_discipline: terracotta is used exactly once per slide as a semantic highlight (the word that matters most), never decoratively scattered — this restraint is a key part of why the system reads premium rather than 'colorful template'.

slide_archetypes.name: Cover / Hook slide
slide_archetypes.frequency: high — first slide of nearly every ai._kid carousel
elements: top-center small mono/serif site label with link glyph, e.g. '🔗 claura-ai.com'
big 2-3 line serif headline in warm-black with exactly one italic terracotta phrase
optional italic serif subhead line below (smaller, warm-black or grey)
optional dark stat pill/bar (e.g. '0 EMPLEADOS | +50 POSTS/SEMANA')
footer: handle bottom-left, short italic terracotta CTA bottom-right ('los 7 →', 'deslizá →')
pagination dots bottom-center
slide_archetypes.decorative_elements: none beyond the type itself; occasionally a small pixel mascot or a paperclip glyph

slide_archetypes.name: Numbered agent/step detail slide (cream + embedded dark mockup)
slide_archetypes.frequency: very high — the workhorse slide of the whole carousel format
slide_archetypes.layout: top kicker badge, left-aligned headline+body, optional mascot illustration top-right, large dark mockup card spanning full width below
elements: blush-fill kicker badge + mono eyebrow ('01/08 — AGENTE 1 · ICP FINDER' or '01.' + serif word + terracotta dot)
serif headline, 1-2 lines, italic terracotta accent phrase
sans body paragraph, one clause bolded for emphasis
small pixel-mascot sticker with a hand-drawn-style arrow + tiny italic caption ('acá no adivinás')
large rounded dark(#121212) 'app window' card with macOS traffic-light dots, showing a fake product UI: chat log, kanban, table, dashboard, or code terminal — this is the 'proof' beat
row of 2-3 stat callouts below the card: italic terracotta big number + mono uppercase caption
footer: handle + italic 'siguiente →'
slide_archetypes.color_usage: cream + warm-black + terracotta + the dark mockup's own near-black/white/green micro-palette
slide_archetypes.decorative_elements: pixel mascot, hand-drawn arrow, traffic-light dots on mockup window

slide_archetypes.name: Icon-grid slide
slide_archetypes.layout: centered headline block over a 2-row x 4-col (or similar) grid of icons with mono labels
elements: top site label
serif headline + italic terracotta accent, short italic subhead
grid of orange 8-bit pixel-art mascot icons, each doing a different 'job' (binoculars = research, crown = strategy, money bag = landing, magnet = ads), mono label under each
terracotta pill tag beneath the grid summarizing the takeaway ('Todo conectado. Un solo sistema.')
footer: handle + italic 'deslizá →'
slide_archetypes.color_usage: cream + warm-black + terracotta (mascots are mono-orange with black outline/features)
slide_archetypes.decorative_elements: the pixel mascot set itself is the decoration

slide_archetypes.name: CTA / engagement slide
slide_archetypes.frequency: high — always the last slide of the carousel
elements: top site label
big serif question headline with italic terracotta accent word ('¿Lo querés para tu marca?')
either: a blush rounded rectangle containing a bold instruction ('Comentá AGENTES'), or a fully-rounded terracotta CTA pill button with white label
one small supporting sans sentence below
footer: handle + italic 'te espero en comments ↓'
slide_archetypes.decorative_elements: occasionally a small gift-box pixel mascot centered above the headline

slide_archetypes.name: Icon-equation / flow slide
slide_archetypes.layout: centered, very sparse — headline + a horizontal row of icon-glyphs joined by '+' / '=' / '→'
elements: big serif statement headline (sometimes with italic terracotta clause, e.g. 'Contesto cero.')
row of small square icon tiles (WhatsApp green, Claude terracotta asterisk mark, a scale/rules icon, a database icon) joined by plus/equals/arrow glyphs and a bold result label ('CRM automático')
footer: handle + italic 'deslizá →'
slide_archetypes.color_usage: cream + warm-black + terracotta + each icon's own native brand color (WhatsApp green, etc. — these are the only non-palette colors allowed, and only as tiny icon glyphs)
slide_archetypes.decorative_elements: none — this archetype relies entirely on typographic/iconographic restraint

signature_motifs.description: a simple humanoid built from square pixels, solid orange/terracotta fill, two black square eyes, white sticker-style outline with a soft drop shadow (looks die-cut/stickered onto the page). Shown in dozens of poses/props: binoculars, crown, target+arrow, magnet, money bag, gift box, waving. This is the account's core brand character and the single most repeated custom asset.
signature_motifs.do_not_confuse_with: the realistic 3D chunky-render mascot with a snapback cap and headphones belongs to a DIFFERENT account (@francisco.carosia); the LEGO/voxel-brick mascot belongs to the brutalist poster series; a flatter disc-eyed pixel character belongs to @juanbertorello.ia. Keep jers-ia's own mascot distinct from all of these if a mascot is desired at all.

signature_motifs.description: standard Instagram carousel pagination dots, bottom-center, small and unobtrusive — authored content stops above this; it's platform chrome but consistently visually intentional in composition (nothing sits too close to it).

seen in the 'blueprint' sub-series (archetype F) and in the brutalist poster series — small plus-sign or targeting-reticle marks in the four corners, borrowed from print/technical-drawing conventions, reinforcing an 'engineered' feel.

small monospace uppercase labels, either inside a soft blush rounded-rectangle badge ('01/08 — AGENTE 1 · ICP FINDER', ai._kid's own style) or inside a solid black pill ('EL BUILD', 'PASO 1 · EL CEREBRO', the blueprint sub-series style). Always sits directly above the headline.

signature_motifs.motif: Handle bottom-left + italic serif hook bottom-right
signature_motifs.description: the closing footer pattern on virtually every slide: plain bold sans '@handle' on the bottom-left, and a short italic serif engagement hook on the bottom-right ('deslizá →', 'siguiente →', 'te espero en comments ↓'). This pairing is one of the most consistent structural signatures across the whole ai._kid set.

a rounded dark-mode window (macOS-style traffic-light dots) floating with soft shadow on the cream canvas, containing a fabricated but highly specific product UI (chat thread, kanban, CRM table, A/B test dashboard, content calendar). This is the credibility device of the whole system — it's what makes claims feel real/measured rather than hypey.

a pill-shaped button, terracotta fill, white bold label, centered — 'Comentá AGENTES', 'Comentá CRM', 'Comentá PLUGINS'. The single most repeated interactive-looking element, always used to drive a comment-to-DM funnel.

signature_motifs.motif: Exactly-one italic terracotta accent word/phrase per headline
signature_motifs.description: the disciplined restraint of highlighting only one phrase per slide in italic serif + terracotta — never more, never a different color. This is arguably the single highest-leverage rule to copy.

teal_check_explicit: CONFIRMED: no teal appears anywhere in the @ai._kid core system or its closest cousins. The palette is strictly cream / terracotta / warm-black (+ incidental native-app icon colors like WhatsApp green used only as tiny glyphs, and a screenshot of WhatsApp's own teal-green header chrome in one mockup, which is depicted app UI, not an authored brand color). Purple appears twice, only inside embedded dark-mode mockup illustrations, never as a background or text-accent color.
